text:
Maria: Starting a thread to scope a new Grafana dashboard for GPU fleet headroom forecasting and thermal zoning. Need a lightweight WIP for staging by next sprint. Minimal must-haves?

Devon: Must haves: per-rack power draw timeseries, a rack headroom gauge, thermal gradient map (front-to-back), and per-GPU allocation failure counter. Keep panels compact for on-call glance.

Kai: Also include an AZ/region selector. We should roll up metrics by zone label so ops can filter to eg us-west-2a. Add maintenance annotations too (`infra_maintenance{service=\"gpu\"}`).

Anita: For alerts, prefer recording rules + 10-15m `for:` thresholds for power. Proposed tiers:
- Sev2: sustained rack power > 88% for 15m
- Sev1: GPU temp > 90C sustained 3m OR rapid rise (>4C/5m)
- Sev2: allocation_errors{node=} > 4 in 10m
- Sev3: sudden drop in 95p util > 40% (possible throttling)

Anita: Example recording rule ideas (PromQL):
```
# 10m moving avg power per rack
record: rack:gpu_power_watts:10m
expr: avg_over_time(sum by (rack) (nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts)[10m])

# 95p util per-rack over 15m window
record: rack:gpu_util_95p:15m
expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, nvidia_gpu_utilization[15m])
```

Devon: For the thermal zoning map, instead of per-GPU we can aggregate front/back/cpu-shelf zones using `gpu_position` label. Heatmap should show gradient and small sparkline per rack.

Ryan: I'll draft the dashboard JSON (name: rack-gpu-headroom-forecast) with these panels:
- Row 1: cluster-at-a-glance (avg util, total power, headroom hrs)
- Row 2: rack power heatmap (rack x 1h), rack headroom gauges
- Row 3: thermal zoning heatmap and top-10 hottest GPUs timeseries
- Row 4: table: tenants by GPU-hours and estimated next-24h cost (using billing_owner label)
- Row 5: alerts & runbook links + quick action to create incident in PagerDuty

Maria: Key ask: headroom forecast ETA. Can we show "hours to saturation" per rack given current queue ingress? Even a rough estimate is useful.

Kai: Rough estimator idea: use `queue_length` metric + mean power per job. Estimator formula:
```
projected_draw_rate_watts = queue_length * job:avg_gpu_power_watts:5m
hours_to_saturation = (rack_capacity_watts - current_draw_watts) / projected_draw_rate_watts / 3600
```
We can implement `job:avg_gpu_power_watts:5m` as a recording rule. Might need smoothing.

Anita: Alerts should reference the estimator but not page on short forecasts. Only page if ETA < 6h AND headroom < 20%. Otherwise send Ops slack notice.

Devon: UX detail: heatmap color thresholds: <60% green, 60-80% amber, 80-92% orange, >92% red. Also show small marker if a rack is on maintenance so ops don't chase false positives.

Ryan: PromQL snippets I'll include on the dashboard README:
```
# current rack headroom (watts)
(rack_power_capacity_watts - sum by (rack) (nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts))

# per-tenant GPU-hours (rolling 24h)
sum by (billing_owner) (increase(gpu_runtime_seconds[24h])) / 3600
```

Ops-bot: quick test: deployed a draft to staging rack-r5 with synthetic workload. Headroom gauge computed hours_to_saturation ~ 4.2h for rack-r5; alert remained a warning (ETA < 6h) but not P1 per policy.

Maria: Nice. Ownership breakdown:
- Ryan: create dashboard JSON + README + screenshots in grafana repo (dashboard name in JSON must match rack-gpu-headroom-forecast)
- Anita: implement recording rules and alert groups; add unit tests for spike suppression
- Devon: heatmap color/UX and retention comparison panels (7d/30d)
- Kai: annotations, region filters, and estimator recording rules
- Ops: run staging validation and simulate failover

Anita: I'll include a throttling-detection rule that looks for correlated CPU steal + util drop + network congestion labels before labeling as throttling. Reduces false positives during infra tests.

Devon: Add a retention row that compares this week vs last week percentiles so we can spot baseline shifts after infra changes.

Grafana-bot: Draft saved to git: grafana/dashboards/rack-gpu-headroom-forecast.json (branch: feature/rack-headroom). CI: lint ok, snapshot recorded.

Maria: Please keep alerts conservative and include runbook links (runbooks/gpu-power-ops.md). Also add a notes panel describing estimator assumptions and known caveats.

Ryan: Will open PR by EOD and add a link to mock data and a query to seed staging. Ping me for mock payloads.

Kai: I'll add an annotation test so maintenance windows render shaded areas in snapshots.

Anita: One final note: for thermal alerts prefer a short `for:` only if derivative(temp) > threshold, otherwise longer window to avoid noisy pages during ramp-up.

Maria: Great. Thanks all. Let's iterate quickly in the PR. :thumbsup:
